title: Hair Loss: The Pits
summary: Josh and Chuck (with Jerry in the production credits) explore hair loss: the three stages of hair growth (anagen, catagen, telogen), and the causes of hair loss including alopecia areata, alopecia totalis and universalis, telogen effluvium (stress, thyroid or iron deficiency, chemotherapy), and androgenetic alopecia (male and female pattern baldness) linked to DHT. They cover the Hamilton-Norwood and Ludwig scales, myths about inheriting baldness from the maternal grandfather, and historical and modern remedies: ancient Egyptian and Hippocratic concoctions, the Crossley Servac and thermocap devices, Capellus litigation, minoxidil (Rogaine), finasteride (Propecia) and its side effects, hair plug and follicular unit extraction transplants, and stem-cell hair growth research. They close with evolutionary theories about baldness and attractiveness. The episode ends with a listener mail about Helen Boss, a distant relative whose car accident caused Sammy Davis Jr. to lose an eye.
topics: Sammy Davis Jr. car accident listener mail

segments.title: Opening banter and hair thinning
segments.summary: Josh and Chuck open with banter about Sinead O'Connor's shaved head and their own thinning hair, and preview the episode's topics.

segments.title: The three stages of hair growth
segments.summary: The hosts explain the anagen, catagen, and telogen phases of the hair cycle, how many hairs are shed daily, and how little science still knows about hair growth.

segments.title: Hair loss across ethnic groups and research funding
segments.summary: They discuss how hair loss is viewed as cosmetic in the West, which has led to less research, and how prevalence differs by ethnic group, with white men losing hair most often.

segments.title: Alopecia and its types
segments.summary: The hosts explain that alopecia is the medical term for any hair loss, and describe alopecia areata, totalis, and universalis, with the etymology traced to the Greek word for fox and Hippocrates.

segments.title: Telogen effluvium and temporary hair loss
segments.summary: Telogen effluvium is described as temporary hair loss triggered by emotional stress, surgery, childbirth, thyroid or iron deficiency. The hosts also cover chemotherapy-related hair loss.

segments.title: Androgenetic alopecia and DHT
segments.summary: Androgenetic alopecia, the most common type, is linked to testosterone converted to DHT by five alpha reductase in follicles. Its occurrence in men and women and the role of DHT in the body are discussed.

segments.title: Hamilton-Norwood scale and the pattern of male baldness
segments.summary: The Hamilton-Norwood scale describes the M-shaped receding hairline and crown balding progression. Examples of actors and celebrities are used. The Ludwig scale for female pattern thinning is also introduced.

segments.title: Family history and baldness myths
segments.summary: The hosts debunk the myth that baldness is inherited only from the maternal grandfather, citing a 2005 German study on the X chromosome, and share anecdotes about family hair. They note that baldness increases with age.

segments.title: Historical and modern baldness remedies
segments.summary: Ancient Egyptian, Hippocratic, Celtic remedies are described, along with 20th century devices like the Crossley Servac and thermocap, and the Capellus lawsuit over clinical claims.
